scope: Binds a set of assets, their credits, their dates and their rights into one 32-byte work root.
note: A complete format on its own terms, developing in its own lane. Nothing in H.SYN.EMA extends, versions, wraps or re-specifies a byte of it, and its evolution is not this format's to direct.

scope: Binds a moving-image work's instruction stream, evidence, derivation graph and compiled timeline under one 32-byte Root State Hash.
relationship: generalises the single-work object into a multiplexed multi-track file
note: In the spec's own words: the extension is unchanged; the interior is opened. Same family discipline — length-prefixed structures, cheapest checks first, a boundary stated on the format's own face — and a different magic, so no reader can confuse one for the other.

scope: The typed vocabulary that populates a SYN coding unit: what an SPS may fix, what an I-Node prompt may say, and what a P-Node delta may legally contain.
note: Additive, not structural. The codec specifies that a director marks an edit seam; it does not specify what a director can say. This fills that, and touches no byte layout.
